projects.title: GlassBox
projects.description: Built a multi-agent lending system where every decision is auditable and every denial comes with a way to fix it, addressing a real gap under ECOA/Reg B, which requires lenders to give specific reasons for a denial rather than a black-box score.7 AI agents (Jac walkers over a provenance graph) assess an application in parallel, then draft a decision. A dedicated No-Discrimination agent reaches its OWN verdict from permissible facts BEFORE seeing the draft, then checks it for reliance on a protected characteristic or a proxy (e.g. ZIP code standing in for race), and can veto in either direction.Key decision: access to protected data is enforced structurally, by graph edge type, not by a prompt — analysts are physically unable to read it, not just asked not to.On a denial, a recourse agent tells the user exactly what to fix, and a Re-check button re-runs the real decision on corrected numbers, so they see a result, not a promise.Stack: Jac for the decision engine, Groq (byLLM) for document reading, Next.js/React frontend. Verdict logic stays fully deterministic.

projects.title: ExoPlanet Hunters
projects.description: Planet Hunters is a machine learning project that uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to help identify possible exoplanets from astronomical light curve data. The goal is to build an assistant that can analyze patterns in star brightness over time and flag signals that may indicate a planet passing in front of its host star.This project combines astronomy, data science, and deep learning. I wanted to explore how artificial intelligence can support real space exploration by helping scientists search through large amounts of telescope data more efficiently.

projects.title: VibeGuard: AI-Powered Sensory Scanner for Inclusive Spaces
projects.description: Hackathon Project (Arduino + OpenCV + Gemini AI) | Nov 2025Built after noticing neurodivergent classmates hesitate outside loud rooms because of sensory overload. VibeGuard reads a room’s “vibe” and gives a simple report so someone can decide whether to walk in.•Hardware: Elegoo UNO R3 with a microphone, PIR motion sensor, and webcam to capture noise, movement, and activity in real time.•Software: a web app using OpenCV and Google Gemini to turn that data into plain mood labels (Calm, Social, Loud, Overwhelming) with confidence scores and coping tips.•Output: scan a space from a laptop or phone, get an instant report plus a QR-log export.

projects.title: SafeHaven: sensor network to connect outreach non-profits with people in need
projects.description: A prototype that helps homeless-outreach non-profits respond faster by flagging activity in public spaces and routing alerts to the nearest partner organization.•Sensor node: Arduino Uno with HC-SR04 ultrasonic and PIR motion sensors to pick up presence and activity, in a low-power, weather-resistant design.•Backend: Python/Flask with OpenCV and AI inference to classify situations (e.g. “person resting,” “possible need”) and trigger location-based alerts to partnered non-profits.•Frontend: a live dashboard (HTML/CSS/JS) where outreach teams get prioritized alerts, map pins, and response logs.

honors_and_awards.description: Awarded for "Piezoelectricity: A Step Towards Cleaner Energy," published in The Harvard Undergraduate Research Journal. honors_and_awards.title: Most Innovative Project Award – VibeGuard

Judges highlighted: "Redefines accessibility with empathy-driven tech."
